text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] service.dns-errors > 30% on geo-dns (prod) — alerting oncall
ana (oncall): got it. seeing timeouts and SERVFAILs for *.prod.rdwd.com from multiple regions (us-east, eu-west). full spike started ~00:03 UTC.
mike: customers reporting unable to reach hosted endpoints, embedding/requests failing. CS triage says ~5 higher-tier customers showing traffic dropoffs.
sarah: quick health check - Route53 records look fine on our side. suspect external resolvers or Cloudflare DNS resolver network?
alex (network): running pings/traceroutes from a few vantage points. initial traceroute to geo-dns-edge.prod.rdwd.com from london -> stalls after Cloudflare layer.
leo: seeing increased TTL expirations and NXDOMAINs from our resolver pool in us-east-1. dig output attached (pasted):
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> @1.1.1.1 geo-dns-edge.prod.rdwd.com
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTH: 0, ADDITIONAL: 1
```
kyra: Cloudflare status shows partial resolver degradation in EU region at 00:02 UTC (their page: https://cloudflarestatus.com). Route53 shows no issues.
jordan-cs: flagged to customers with highest impact, they're asking for ETA. need quick assessment for status page.
nana (oncall): initial mitigation plan: 1) switch geoDNS fallback policy to prefer route53-backend for affected regions 2) lower TTLs 3) enable regional failover to prod-warm (eu fallback) 4) open tickets with Cloudflare + AWS. doing step 1 now.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued: geo-router config change (id: cfg-7632) by ana. manual approval required.
mike: approve, do it. we need to shift traffic before more customers degrade.
nana (oncall): applying config, patching geodns policy to prefer route53-backend for eu and apac (curl below):
```
curl -X POST "https://geo-api.redwood.internal/v1/policies/cfg-7632/apply" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -d '{"regions": ["eu-west-1","ap-southeast-1"], "preference": "route53"}'
```
leo: rolling now. watch logs.
(small pause)
nana (oncall): change applied. monitoring. RTT and success rate improving for some checks.
alex (network): still seeing intermittent SERVFAILs from specific Cloudflare resolver ASN 13335 for us-east prefixes — looks like selective packet drop / rate limiting on their side. opened ticket to Cloudflare (ticket CF-987654). included dig/traceroute + timestamps.
kyra: raised AWS support case inc-aws-5421 to confirm Route53 propagation and any anomalies.
mike: status page draft: "We are investigating elevated DNS resolution errors affecting some customers in EU/APAC. Mitigation in progress; routing traffic to alternate DNS backend. Impact: intermittent request failures to hosted inference. Next update in 15 minutes." anyone object?
jordan-cs: fine. include affected customer list note (internal only).
leo: logs show failure rate dropped from 34% -> 9% for eu probes after switch. us-east still ~18% due to unresolved Cloudflare resolver path.
sarah: recommend we also lower TTL for the affected records to 30s to speed client failover while this is ongoing. I'll prepare script.
nana (oncall): doing TTL change now.
nana (oncall): TTLs set to 30s on geo records. monitor for propagation effects.
alex (network): Cloudflare replied: "we're seeing congestion on resolver nodes impacting some queries, working on mitigation. We'll post update in 20m."
mike: good. keep monitoring. assign on-call handoff if this lasts > 2h.
leo: one oddity: some enterprise customers using corporate resolvers are caching SERVFAIL responses — we should add guidance for engineers to retry with fresh resolver or explicit DNS-over-HTTPS. Jordan, can CS push that note?
jordan-cs: yes, sending to impacted customer contacts now: suggested workaround: flush resolver cache, switch to Google/Cloudflare public resolvers temporarily, or retry after 30s.
stats snapshot pasted:
```
region | pre-mit %errors | post-mit %errors
EU     | 35%            | 9%
APAC   | 31%            | 8%
US-E   | 18%            | 17%
```
mike: looks like mitigation mostly working for EU/APAC. US-E persistent. next steps: 1) escalate to Cloudflare network team with BGP/traceroute artifacts (alex) 2) keep Route53 fallback in place 3) status page update in 15m (mike) 4) prepare for automated rollback of geo-router policy if regressions.
nana (oncall): I'll continue watching for 30m then hand off to night oncall if stable. if error rate spikes >25% again, we'll reopen bridge.
kyra: coordinating with Cloudflare. asked for estimated time to fix and whether they plan to re-balance resolver load or route around problem nodes.
alex (network): added BGP path and pcap evidence to CF ticket. also confirmed no internal rate-limiting on our side.
leo: reminding — capture PCAPs and dig logs for postmortem. I'll own the evidence collection.
jordan-cs: customers contacted, some asked for credit/impact windows. we need preliminary SLO impact estimate. can eng produce token-level failure count for last 2 hours?
mike: Leo can run token/error counts; Leo?
leo: running query now, will paste numbers in 10m.
sarah: small ask — add a canary check for resolver health into our observability to catch Cloudflare resolver ASN anomalies next time.
nana (oncall): noted, add to incidents followups.
(statusbot): Status page updated: "Investigating: DNS resolution errors affecting some regions. Mitigation in progress (routing to alternate DNS backend)."
(more monitoring)
nana (oncall): 20m update: EU/APAC stable, US-E errate down to 12%. Cloudflare says they are mitigating and seeing improvement. keeping status page up.
mike: if Cloudflare confirms fix, we should plan a controlled revert to primary geo-router policy after 1h of stable metrics and gradually increase weight.
kyra: CF update: "resolver cluster healthy, cache warms expected. continuing monitoring."
nana (oncall): leaving note for handoff: if error rate stays <10% across regions, close incident after 2 hours and file postmortem. primary owners: ana (incident lead), alex (network), leo (evidence/metrics), sarah (observability).
jordan-cs: CS will prepare customer-impact summary for postmortem.
mike: thanks all. nice quick coordination. pulling on-call calendar to schedule postmortem.
leo: pasted token error counts (last 2h): total requests 3,421,889; failed requests 74,321 (~2.17% global), concentrated in EU/APAC windows.
nana (oncall): incident resolved: no major regressions in last 2 hours, closing pager. followups assigned in #postmortems.
incident-bot: Pager closed: incident incident-2026-1792500000 (owner: ana)
